answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a cooling-off period before it may earn reputation or influence votes. A vine of linked accounts then ties up capital in every branch, while delayed eligibility prevents an attacker from rapidly cycling funds through fresh personas. If one identity is caught gaming the system, a ripple of slashed collateral makes the whole campaign costly; the attacker must risk more capital and wait longer to wander back under another name.
